one_liner: Portable C11 in-place WebAssembly interpreter with eager validation; instantiates modules about 90x faster than single-threaded Wasmtime/Wasmer Cranelift.
what_it_does: Toywasm is a WebAssembly 2.0 interpreter written in C11, with optional SIMD, threads, tail calls, exception handling, multi-memory, WASI preview1, wasi-threads and dynamic linking. You can run it as the toywasm command, or link its static libraries through CMake find_package. The C API is its own, not Wasmtime's or the wasm-c-api: load_context plus module_create, then instance_create with an import_object chain, then instance_execute_func with instance_execute_handle_restart. It is not a drop-in for any JIT runtime.
how_it_is_fast: Startup is cheap because nothing is compiled. The module is decoded and validated eagerly, then executed in place from the read-only bytecode. Validation leaves only small side annotations: a jump table for forward branches (searched by binary search, with a 4-entry jump cache), local and result-type cell-index tables, and value-size annotations for value-polymorphic instructions. A Cranelift JIT instead has to generate machine code for every function. For execution it uses per-instruction handler functions chained with clang's musttail attribute, plus a locals cache and fast paths, and it deliberately avoids huge-switch and computed-goto dispatch.
when_to_use: You load large or many modules and run only a little of each, so instantiation latency dominates. In wasmi-benchmarks on EPYC 7763 it starts ffmpeg in about 211 ms, while Wasmtime Cranelift, built there without parallel compilation, is about 90x slower over the startup geomean.
Hosts where a JIT is not allowed or not available: microcontrollers via NuttX (esp32), wasm32-wasi (toywasm runs on itself), i386, arm64, riscv64, NetBSD and Windows (core wasm only).

Embedders who want a small, readable C codebase under BSD-2-Clause with broad proposal coverage (SIMD, threads, EH, tail-call, custom page sizes) and a low memory footprint. The author's ffmpeg startup run peaks at about 40 MB RSS, against 200-550 MB for Wasmtime and Wasmer.
Sandboxing where read-only module mapping, restartable execution, timeouts (--timeout) and heap-usage limits (--max-memory) matter more than raw speed.
when_not_to_use: Compute-heavy work. In the author's own ffmpeg run it takes 65.0 s, against 18.4 s for Wasm3 and 23.1 s for the WAMR fast interpreter, and the JITs take 3.5-11.9 s. In wasmi-benchmarks its execution geomean is x318.96, the slowest of the runtimes.

When startup is all that matters, lazy runtimes start faster: Wasm3 (lazy) is x2.77 and Wasmi lazy is x1.37-1.56, against toywasm x18.35. V8 starts ffmpeg and spidermonkey faster. On the author's MacBook the WAMR classic interpreter starts as fast (0.19 s vs 0.18 s).
Projects that need a stable API or ABI: the README lists both as non-goals, and version numbers are not semver.
Builds with GCC or MSVC: the musttail dispatch is enabled only under clang (platform.h). The README recommends clang with LTO, so other compilers produce a slower interpreter.
Wasm GC, the component model, or full WASI on Windows: GC is an open request (#282), and Windows supports core wasm only.

integration.dependencies: none for the core library. libc and POSIX are needed for WASI; wabt and cmocka are needed only for the tests; littlefs is optional.
integration.min_toolchain: C11 and CMake. Clang with musttail (LLVM 13 or later) and LTO is recommended for speed; release binaries are built with clang and ThinLTO.
integration.platforms: Tested on CI: macOS amd64, Ubuntu amd64, i386, arm64 and riscv64 (the last two under qemu), Windows x64 (core wasm only) and wasm32-wasi. Tested manually: NuttX (esp32, sim) and NetBSD. armhf and s390x CI is disabled.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented as a guarantee. Modules are mapped read-only and never modified (README). A build with TOYWASM_ENABLE_WASM_THREADS runs wasi-threads with shared memories, and each thread uses its own exec_context.

gotchas: Harness flaw behind the execution caveat: wasmi-benchmarks builds toywasm through the toywasmx cc-crate build script, and its Linux CI sets CC=gcc-15 (.github/actions/install-dependencies). toywasm's platform.h defines __HAVE_MUSTTAIL only when __clang__ is defined, so under gcc INSN_SUCCESS falls back to returning to the dispatch loop after every instruction. The C code also gets no LTO, because the Cargo profile's lto=fat covers Rust only. That probably explains why toywasm runs about 18.7x slower than WAMR fast-interp on EPYC (gcc), against about 8.7x on Apple M2 Pro (macOS, where cc is presumably Apple clang, so musttail is on) and 3.5x slower than Wasm3 in the author's own clang build (derived from page data). The startup claim is not affected in toywasm's disfavour.

Harness flaw on the baseline side: rt-wasmtime is built with default-features = false (features runtime and anyhow only), so it has no parallel-compilation feature and Cranelift compiles single-threaded. Real Wasmtime first runs use many threads: the author's ffmpeg startup shows 40.94 s user against 4.87 s real. The x1634 Wasmtime ratio is therefore inflated, though toywasm still wins on startup by a wide margin.

Annotations cost memory. On ffmpeg (15.4 MB of code) they add about 3.1 MB: a 2.4 MB jump table plus the type and cell-index tables. Disabling them (--disable-jump-table and the cellidx options) makes execution about 10x slower (624 s against 65 s on ffmpeg).

Pointer arithmetic on NULL in empty vectors trips UBSan pointer-overflow, and the build disables that sanitizer (issue #362, Sep 2026, raised by the nanowasm R package). Out-of-memory sometimes returns ENOMEM and sometimes traps (#258).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Wasm3 or WAMR when you want a smaller, cleaner C codebase with eager validation and read-only in-place execution, newer proposals (EH, tail-call, threads, custom page sizes) and a low RSS, and can accept 3-4x slower compute. Fizzy starts about as fast (x17.83), but its catalogue entry says it is WebAssembly 1.0 only and has had no code changes since 2023, whereas toywasm is maintained and covers WASI. Use Wasm3 or the WAMR fast interpreter when execution speed matters.
verified_claims_summary: wasmi-benchmarks times compile plus instantiate of 7 modules, from erc20 to ffmpeg, on an AMD EPYC 7763 GitHub Actions runner, with toywasm built by gcc-15 via the toywasmx 0.2 crate. Toywasm's startup geomean is x18.35 against the per-case fastest runtime, versus x1634.19 for Wasmtime Cranelift and x1484.15 for Wasmer Cranelift; Wasmtime was compiled without parallel compilation. The win holds on all five CPU data sets, but it is startup-only.
status_note: Active single-maintainer project (last commit 2026-08-01, 119 stars, 3,109 commits, 13 open issues) under BSD-2-Clause, small and portable enough to vendor (NuttX apps and the nanowasm R package already embed it), but its API and ABI are explicitly unstable.
